Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 10 May 1983, after the draft finalized by the Lubricants and Related Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council.

0.2 Antiwear hydraulic oils are generally used for the lubrication of These oils are especially required axial, piston, vane and gear pumps. in systems where both piston and vane pumps are used for heavy duty These oils may also be used for lubricating light loaded gears service. These oils are not intended for use in hydraulic systems and bearinos containing bsiiver plated components. 0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordThe number of significant places retained in ance with IS : 2-1960*. the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and methods of sampling and test for antiwear hydraulic oil intended for use in all axial, piston, vane and gear pumps.
2. GRADES

2.1 The material

shall be available in five viscosity 32, VG 46, VG 68, VG 100 and VG 150.

REQUIREMENTS 3.1 General - The material shall be made from refined mineral base stocks of high viscosity index and shall contain suitable additives to give satisfactory performance. It shall be clear and free from xvater, dirt and suspended impurities. 3.2 The material shall also comply with the requirements when tested according to the methods prescribed IS : 1448*. shall be packed in containers of metal or any other as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.

4.2 The containers shall be securely closed and marked with the name of grade and mass of the material; recognized the manufacturer; name, trade-mark, if any; and identification in code or otherwise to enable the lot of consignment or manufacture to be traced back. 4.2.1 The containers may also be marked with Standard Mark.

4.2.2 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of Bureau of Indian Sritlldsrds Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thcreundcr. A-l.1 This method determines the conlpatibility of petroleum oils with nitrilc rubber seal material in terms of change in volume percent and shore hardness. A-2. DEFINITION

A-2.1 Percent Volume Change - It is the difference between the volume of the nitrile rubber specimen before and after the test and its ratio to the volume before the test started, multiplied by 100. A-2.2 Change in Shore Hardness men - It is the difference in hardness determined by shore hardness tester. 6 of Nitrile Rubber Specibetween the initial and after test

PROCEDURE A-5.1 Use three rubber test specimens, weigh each piece in air to the nearest milligram (Ml) and then reweigh each test piece in distilled water (Mz) at the standard laboratory temperature, care being taken to ensure that all air bubbles are removed, Formation of air bubbles may be avoided by dipping the test piece momentarily into a suitable liquid such as methyl alcohol. A-5.2 Blot the test pieces does not deposit lint. dry with filter paper or piece of textile that of

A-5.4 Immerse the rubber test specimens vertically and keep them separate in the glass jar containing petroleum oil. The amount of oil should be at least 15 times the combined volume of the test pieces and sufficient Replace the sttoper and put the jar and to keep them totally immersed. contents in test oven for 100 hours at 80 & 2�C.
